name: OpenEvidence
desc: Medical AI search and answer tool that gives clinicians evidence from peer-reviewed literature, funded by advertising.
markets: Used by physicians in the United States; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Brand reaches US doctors, a niche audience; limited consumer or international relevance, though pharma advertisers could be hosted as B2B guests.

name: Physical Intelligence
desc: Develops foundation models for general-purpose robot control, aimed at letting robots perform varied physical tasks.
markets: Research-stage company based in the US; no known commercial customers or international operations.
rationale: Research-stage B2B firm with no consumer brand; a technology-showcase tie-in is conceivable but weak.

name: Prime Data Centers
desc: Develops and operates purpose-built, high-density data centers for hyperscalers and enterprises in the United States.
markets: Campuses in US markets such as Los Angeles, Chicago and Virginia; no verified operations abroad.
rationale: Infrastructure supplier selling to hyperscale customers; F1 hospitality could help B2B relationships, but there is no consumer brand and a domestic footprint.

name: Saviynt
desc: Cloud identity security platform for identity governance, access management and privileged access, sold to enterprises.
markets: Enterprise customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific through direct sales and partners.
rationale: Enterprise security vendor with global customers; F1 hospitality and technology partnerships suit cybersecurity peers like CrowdStrike and Zscaler already in the sport.

name: Shengshu Technology
desc: Chinese generative AI company best known for the Vidu text-to-video model, founded in Beijing in 2023.
markets: Based in China; Vidu is offered to creators online, and I cannot verify overseas operations.
rationale: Video-generation brand could showcase technology through F1 content, but Chinese AI firms face market-access limits and its overseas footprint is unverified.

name: Socure
desc: Identity verification and fraud prevention platform using AI and data for banks, fintechs, telecoms and government agencies.
markets: Customers mainly in the United States; I cannot verify significant operations in other regions.
rationale: B2B fraud-prevention vendor to banks and fintechs, many of which sponsor F1; hospitality value is real but the brand is unknown to the public.

name: V.tal
desc: Neutral digital infrastructure company providing wholesale fibre, backhaul and network services to telecom operators in Brazil.
markets: Operates fibre networks in Brazil serving telecom operators; no known operations in other countries.
rationale: Wholesale network provider with no consumer brand; Brazil-only footprint, though the Sao Paulo Grand Prix could suit operator hospitality.

name: Waabi
desc: Autonomous trucking technology company building the Waabi Driver with a generative AI simulator, founded in 2021.
markets: Testing and pilots in North America, mainly Texas and Canada; no verified operations elsewhere.
rationale: Autonomous-driving technology showcase fits F1's engineering image, but the company is early-stage with a freight-customer base and little marketing culture.

name: Xanadu
desc: Builds photonic quantum computers and maintains the PennyLane quantum software library for researchers and enterprises.
markets: Toronto-based; PennyLane has users worldwide and research partners in several regions.
rationale: Deep-tech brand that could use F1 as a technology showcase, but customers are researchers and a niche enterprise audience.

name: XPENG Robotics
desc: Robotics business of Chinese EV maker XPENG, developing humanoid robots such as the Iron humanoid.
markets: Part of XPENG, based in Guangzhou; commercial humanoid sales and overseas plans are unverified.
rationale: Technology showcase is possible via parent XPENG, which sells cars in Europe, but the robotics unit is early-stage.

name: Safaricom
desc: Kenya's largest mobile operator, offering voice, data, broadband and the M-Pesa mobile money service in Kenya and Ethiopia.
markets: Operates in Kenya and Ethiopia; M-Pesa is a core product with wide East African presence.
rationale: Strong consumer brand in East Africa, but with no F1 race in the region; hospitality and brand-awareness fit is modest.

name: Zuoyebang
desc: Chinese online education company behind a homework-help app and AI learning devices for K-12 students.
markets: Customers are students and parents in China; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Consumer education brand with a China-focused audience; F1 fit is limited and restricted by its domestic market.

name: Spotify
desc: Audio streaming service offering music, podcasts and audiobooks to free and paying subscribers worldwide.
markets: Available in about 180 markets across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, Africa and the Middle East.
rationale: Mass-market global brand with music and culture ties that match F1's entertainment-led audience growth and fan-content programmes.

name: Flipkart Marketplace
desc: Marketplace entity of Flipkart, the Indian e-commerce group, listing third-party sellers who sell to consumers.
markets: Sells to consumers across India; the group is majority-owned by Walmart.
rationale: Large Indian consumer brand and F1 has a growing Indian fan base, but there is no India race and the business is domestic.

name: Animoca Brands
desc: Digital entertainment and blockchain company with a large portfolio of Web3 gaming and metaverse investments.
markets: Based in Hong Kong with investments and partnerships across Asia, Europe and North America.
rationale: Web3 and gaming brand seeking mainstream audiences; F1's digital fan engagement offers a showcase, though crypto marketing is regulated in some markets.

name: Tekion
desc: Cloud platform for automotive retail offering dealer management, CRM, finance and service software to dealerships and OEMs.
markets: Customers are car dealers and manufacturers, mainly in North America; I know of no large overseas base.
rationale: Automotive-industry software supplier whose dealer and OEM customers overlap with F1 manufacturers; B2B hospitality is a clear use.

name: Life360
desc: Family safety app providing location sharing, crash detection and driving safety, plus Tile item trackers.
markets: Users in many countries, mostly United States; Tile devices are sold internationally.
rationale: Consumer app with driving-safety features and a mass audience; F1 could support international subscriber growth and brand awareness.

name: Triller
desc: Social video app with AI-assisted music videos that also hosts live boxing and combat sports events.
markets: US-based app with users abroad; I cannot verify its current operating footprint.
rationale: Consumer entertainment brand seeking attention, but its corporate and listing situation is uncertain and may limit partnership credibility.

name: Tempo
desc: Payments-focused Layer 1 blockchain incubated by Stripe, built for stablecoin payments.
markets: US-based network with payment and bank partners from several regions; production use is early.
rationale: Stripe, its incubator, is an F1 partner, so payments positioning fits, but Tempo is a new infrastructure brand.

name: Qihoo 360 Technology
desc: Chinese internet security company offering antivirus software, a browser, search and mobile security, moving toward AI.
markets: Consumer base is in China; overseas business is small and I cannot verify it.
rationale: Known Chinese brand with consumer reach, but F1 fit is limited by its domestic focus.
changed: Taken private in 2018, relisted via 360 Security Technology in Shanghai

name: BT
desc: UK broadband, mobile and fixed-line operator with consumer brands BT, EE and Plusnet, plus business and network divisions.
markets: Core UK operations plus global business services for multinational customers across several regions.
rationale: Strong UK consumer brand with a sports-sponsorship history; F1 offers UK Grand Prix presence and corporate hospitality for business customers.

name: London Stock Exchange Group
desc: Financial markets infrastructure and data group operating the London Stock Exchange, LCH clearing and FTSE Russell indices.
markets: Operates exchanges, clearing and data services for customers across Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Global capital-markets brand with a B2B client base; F1 hospitality suits client entertainment, though Nasdaq is already a partner.

name: Palantir Technologies
desc: Data integration and analytics software, including Foundry and AIP platforms, sold to governments and large commercial customers.
markets: Customers in the United States, Europe and Asia across government and commercial sectors.
rationale: Enterprise AI brand with high profile and a technology-showcase fit with F1's data use, but defence work may complicate brand-safety.

name: GoDaddy
desc: Domain registrar and web services provider selling hosting, website builder, security and email tools to small businesses.
markets: Customers in the US, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America through local-language sites.
rationale: Mass-market consumer and small-business brand with international reach and past sports advertising; F1 could drive awareness across several regions.

name: Harvey
desc: Generative AI platform for law firms and corporate legal teams to draft, review and research documents.
markets: Customers are large law firms and legal departments in the US, UK and Europe.
rationale: B2B professional-services AI brand; F1 hospitality could suit law-firm clients, but there is little consumer awareness.

name: RLDatix
desc: Healthcare software provider for patient safety, incident and risk management, governance and workforce scheduling.
markets: Customers are hospitals and health systems in North America, the UK, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B healthcare software with little brand marketing; hospitality value is limited because customers are health-system buyers.

name: Walgreens Boots Alliance
desc: Pharmacy and retail healthcare group operating Walgreens and Boots stores, plus pharmaceutical wholesale and care businesses.
markets: Stores in the United States, United Kingdom and Europe, plus wholesale operations in several countries.
rationale: Very visible consumer retail brand in the US and UK, both big F1 markets; a health and beauty sponsorship could suit.
changed: Taken private by Sycamore Partners in 2025

name: Wiz
desc: Cloud security platform that scans cloud environments to find and prioritize risks for enterprises.
markets: Enterprise customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; large research base in Israel.
rationale: Fast-growing cybersecurity brand; F1 peers like CrowdStrike and Zscaler show the category fits, and Google parent is already a partner.
changed: Acquisition by Google announced in 2025, reported completed in 2026
f1: Parent Google is a current F1 partner

name: Zebra Technologies
desc: Maker of barcode scanners, printers, mobile computers and software for retail, logistics and healthcare operations.
markets: Sells through channel partners to customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Enterprise hardware brand serving retail and logistics clients; F1 hospitality suits business customers, and technology partnerships are plausible.

name: 4Paradigm
desc: Enterprise AI company selling machine learning platforms and decision-intelligence software to large organizations.
markets: Customers mainly in China, with some Asia-Pacific activity I cannot verify.
rationale: B2B AI vendor with little consumer profile and China focus; F1 value would be a limited technology showcase.

name: Applied Intuition
desc: Software for simulation, validation and vehicle operating systems used to develop autonomous and software-defined vehicles.
markets: Customers include automakers and defence agencies in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Automotive-engineering software with real overlap with F1 manufacturers; strong B2B hospitality and technology-showcase fit.

name: Dataminr
desc: Real-time event detection company that uses AI to scan public data and alert corporate and public-sector customers.
markets: Customers in the United States, Europe and elsewhere across corporate, news and government sectors.
rationale: Real-time data brand with a technology link to F1 broadcasting and risk monitoring; B2B hospitality use, little consumer awareness.

name: Deel
desc: Global HR and payroll platform to hire, pay and manage employees and contractors in many countries.
markets: Serves companies and workers in more than 150 countries across all major regions.
rationale: Global business-software brand with high marketing spend and international customers; F1's global audience matches its aims.

name: Didi Woya
desc: Beijing company developing autonomous driving technology, apparently linked to the Didi ride-hailing group.
markets: Based in Beijing; no verified customers or operations outside China.
rationale: Autonomous-driving developer with unclear structure and a China focus; F1 fit is speculative.

name: Docusign
desc: Electronic signature and agreement management software sold to businesses and individuals.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific across many industries.
rationale: Established business brand with international customers; F1 hospitality fits enterprise relationship building and fits tech sponsors already in the sport.

name: Figma
desc: Collaborative interface design tool for product teams, with FigJam whiteboards and developer tools.
markets: Used by teams worldwide, with large user bases in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Design brand with a creative community and a global audience; F1 offers a strong design and technology showcase.

name: Keysight Technologies
desc: Electronic design and test measurement company serving communications, automotive and aerospace customers.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia in communications, automotive and aerospace.
rationale: Engineering brand whose automotive test business and B2B customers fit F1 technology partnerships and hospitality.

name: KoBold Metals
desc: Mineral exploration company using AI and geoscience data to find critical minerals such as copper, nickel and lithium.
markets: Exploration projects in several countries including Zambia and the United States.
rationale: Battery-metals supply story fits F1's sustainability goals, but it is an exploration business with few consumers.

name: Mavenir
desc: Telecom software company building cloud-native and Open RAN network software for mobile operators, including 5G core.
markets: Sells to mobile operators across North America, Europe, Asia and other regions.
rationale: Telecom-equipment supplier to operators, some of which sponsor F1; limited consumer brand but credible B2B hospitality use.

name: Megvii
desc: Computer vision and AI company known for Face++ recognition and smart city, logistics and consumer applications.
markets: Business is centred in China; I cannot verify significant overseas operations.
rationale: AI vision brand with a China focus and sensitive face-recognition reputation; F1 fit is weak.

name: Momenta
desc: Autonomous driving software company building driver-assistance and self-driving systems with offices in China and Europe.
markets: Offices in China and Munich; supplies automakers including some European and Japanese brands.
rationale: Automotive-technology showcase suits F1, with carmaker customers who attend races; B2B supplier brand with low public awareness.

name: Perplexity
desc: AI answer engine that retrieves web results and generates cited answers for consumers and businesses.
markets: Consumer and enterprise users across many countries, with partnerships with telecom and device companies.
rationale: Fast-growing consumer AI brand needing awareness; F1's global digital audience and tech sponsors make a good showcase.

name: Pony.ai
desc: Autonomous driving company running robotaxi services and developing self-driving trucks and vehicle technology.
markets: Robotaxi operations in Chinese cities, with pilots and partnerships in the Middle East, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Mobility technology brand with international expansion; F1 suits a showcase in Gulf and European markets.

name: Revvity
desc: Life sciences and diagnostics company providing instruments, reagents and testing services; formerly PerkinElmer.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia, sold to labs, pharma and healthcare providers.
rationale: B2B science brand with international customers; hospitality could serve clients but there is little consumer marketing.

name: Superhuman (formerly Grammarly)
desc: AI productivity company combining the Grammarly writing assistant with the Superhuman email client and Coda.
markets: Consumers and businesses across many countries, with Grammarly widely used in English-speaking markets.
rationale: Mass consumer software brand with large marketing spend; F1's global audience offers awareness across several regions.

name: Chainguard
desc: Software supply chain security company selling hardened container images, libraries and tools to enterprises.
markets: US-based; customers are enterprises, and I cannot verify specific overseas operations.
rationale: Developer-security vendor with a niche audience; F1 hospitality suits security peers already in the sport, but brand awareness is low.

name: Cohesity
desc: Data security and management company selling backup, recovery, ransomware protection and AI data tools.
markets: Enterprise customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Enterprise data-protection brand with global customers; F1 offers B2B hospitality and a tech-sponsor peer group.
changed: Merged with Veritas data protection business in 2024

name: Commvault
desc: Data protection and cyber resilience software providing backup, recovery and data management for enterprises.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; sells data protection to enterprises and public bodies worldwide.
rationale: Enterprise software brand with a global customer base; F1 hospitality and cyber-resilience messaging suit its audience.

name: Cybereason
desc: Cybersecurity company offering endpoint detection and response, extended detection and response and managed threat hunting.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; operations in Israel and Japan.
rationale: Cybersecurity brand of the kind already in F1, but now part of a larger group and with limited independent budget.

name: Gen
desc: Consumer cyber safety company behind Norton, Avast, LifeLock and other security and identity protection products.
markets: Consumers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific through retail and online sales.
rationale: Mass-market consumer security brands with a global audience; F1 suits a protection and trust message.
changed: Formed in 2022 from NortonLifeLock and Avast merger

name: Heartflow
desc: Medical technology company that creates 3D coronary artery models from CT scans to support heart disease diagnosis.
markets: Sold to hospitals in the United States, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Clinical device business selling to hospitals; F1 fit is limited to a technology showcase.

name: HyperVault AI Data Center
desc: Indian AI data centre business offering hosting and compute for artificial intelligence workloads.
markets: Based in Mumbai; details of customers and any operations abroad are unverified.
rationale: Infrastructure start-up with unclear ownership and a domestic focus; F1 relevance is weak.

name: Luma AI
desc: Generative AI company developing 3D capture and video generation models, including Dream Machine and Ray.
markets: Consumer and professional users in many countries through apps and online tools.
rationale: Creative-AI brand that could showcase video generation through F1 content; a creator audience is a fit.

name: Transdev
desc: Public transport operator running bus, tram, rail and on-demand mobility services for cities and authorities.
markets: Operates in Europe, North America, Australia, Asia and Africa under contracts with public authorities.
rationale: Contracts come from public authorities, so consumer marketing value is limited; hospitality could build city relationships.

name: Uniphore
desc: Enterprise AI company selling conversational AI and automation for customer service and sales teams.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia, with major development in Chennai, India.
rationale: Enterprise AI vendor with customers in banking and telecom; hospitality suits customer relationships.

name: Upland Software
desc: Cloud software provider offering work management, digital engagement and marketing tools to enterprises.
markets: Customers across North America and Europe, sold through direct sales.
rationale: Small enterprise software group with limited marketing budget; F1 cost is likely high for its scale.

name: Weimob
desc: Cloud commerce and marketing software provider offering social e-commerce tools to merchants in China.
markets: Serves merchants in China; no verified significant overseas operations.
rationale: Chinese merchant-software vendor with a domestic customer base and little international brand activity; limited F1 fit.

name: Digi Power X
desc: Digital infrastructure company that grew from bitcoin mining toward AI cloud and high-performance computing.
markets: Operations in North America; I cannot verify customers or operations in other regions.
rationale: Small infrastructure firm with limited brand marketing; compute and crypto angles are weak for F1.

name: GD Culture Group
desc: Nasdaq-listed company pursuing livestreaming and AI-driven digital human businesses from a New York base.
markets: US-based; the scope of its operations and any customers abroad are unverified.
rationale: Micro-cap with an unclear business, so a sponsorship at F1 scale is unrealistic.

name: LayerZero Labs
desc: Blockchain infrastructure company that created the LayerZero protocol for interoperability between blockchains.
markets: Protocol used by crypto applications worldwide; the company is based in Vancouver.
rationale: Crypto-infrastructure brand with a developer audience; F1 already has several crypto partners, though regulation can limit marketing.

name: Odeko
desc: Supplies and software for independent coffee shops and cafes, including ordering, inventory and payment tools.
markets: Serves independent cafes in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: Domestic B2B supplier with a small-business customer base; limited F1 relevance beyond niche coffee-brand activation.

name: Roc360
desc: Real estate finance platform and parent of Roc Capital, lending to residential real estate investors.
markets: Lends to US residential investors; no known international operations.
rationale: US lender with a niche professional borrower base; F1 fit is weak.

name: Wispr Flow
desc: AI voice dictation software that turns speech into polished text across apps and devices.
markets: Consumer and professional users online; I cannot verify specific country footprints.
rationale: Consumer productivity app seeking awareness; F1 offers global reach but a start-up budget is limited.

name: Felix
desc: Fintech that lets Latino immigrants in the United States send money to family in Latin America through chat apps.
markets: US senders paying to recipients in Latin America via WhatsApp-style chat apps.
rationale: Remittance brand targeting US Latino communities; Mexico, Miami and Austin races match its audience, though budget is small.

name: Upwork
desc: Online freelance marketplace connecting businesses with independent professionals for project work, based in the San Francisco Bay Area.
markets: Clients and freelancers across North America, Europe, Asia and other regions.
rationale: Global marketplace brand with awareness goals; F1 offers business-audience hospitality and global exposure.

name: Swvl
desc: Mass-transit mobility company with an app for booking seats on shared fixed-route buses and private rides.
markets: Operates in the Middle East and Africa, originally from Egypt, with Gulf headquarters.
rationale: Gulf-based consumer mobility brand; Abu Dhabi and Saudi races are close to its region, though its scale is modest.

name: MegazoneCloud
desc: Korean cloud and digital transformation company reselling AWS, Microsoft and Google cloud services with managed services.
markets: Based in Seoul with operations in Asia and the United States; customers are enterprises.
rationale: B2B cloud reseller; as AWS, Google and Microsoft are F1 partners, hospitality may interest it but brand awareness is limited.

name: Oura
desc: Health technology company making the Oura Ring, a smart ring tracking sleep, activity and readiness.
markets: Rings sold online and through retailers in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Wearable health brand with a performance-minded audience, matching WHOOP, already an F1 partner, and a clear technology showcase.

name: Lovable
desc: AI software platform that lets users build web apps and websites by describing them in natural language.
markets: Users worldwide building apps online; founded in Stockholm in 2023.
rationale: Fast-growing AI brand seeking global awareness; F1 offers reach, and AI companies already sponsor the sport.

name: Neko Health
desc: Health-tech company offering full-body scans with sensors and AI to give people preventive health reports.
markets: Clinics in Sweden and the United Kingdom, with expansion to other cities.
rationale: Consumer health brand seeking awareness in UK and Europe, both strong F1 markets; wellness and performance angle suits.

name: Abridge
desc: Ambient AI that listens to doctor-patient conversations and generates clinical notes for health systems.
markets: Customers are health systems in the United States; I know of limited overseas activity.
rationale: B2B healthcare AI sold to hospitals; hospitality has some value, but customers are US health systems.

name: Angle Health
desc: Health insurance technology company selling self-funded health plans and administration software to employers.
markets: Serves employers in the United States only; no known international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: US employer-benefits business with no international audience or consumer marketing culture; F1 fit is weak.

name: Aura
desc: Consumer digital safety company offering identity theft protection, credit monitoring, VPN, antivirus and parental controls.
markets: Sells subscriptions to consumers in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: Heavy consumer advertiser, but its audience is US-only; F1 fit is plausible for the US races.

name: Coalition
desc: Cyber insurance and security company offering policies and security tools in the US, Canada and the UK.
markets: Sells cyber insurance in the US, Canada and the UK.
rationale: Insurer with a cyber-risk brand; F1 hospitality fits broker relationships, and the UK and US races align with its markets.

name: Consensus Cloud Solutions
desc: Provider of secure digital document exchange and fax services, including eFax, for healthcare and business users.
markets: Customers in North America and Europe, with eFax used in many countries.
rationale: Mature B2B software firm with modest marketing budget; F1 fit is weak.
changed: Spun off from J2 Global in 2021

name: Earendil Labs
desc: Biotechnology company applying artificial intelligence to drug discovery, per its Crunchbase profile.
markets: Listed address in Delaware; I cannot verify operations or partners.
rationale: Early-stage drug discovery company with no consumer brand; F1 relevance is weak.

name: EliseAI
desc: Conversational AI software automating leasing, tenant communication and patient scheduling for property managers and healthcare providers.
markets: Customers in the United States, with some expansion into other markets I cannot verify.
rationale: B2B vertical software for landlords and clinics; F1 hospitality offers limited value.

name: Elm
desc: Saudi digital solutions company building government and enterprise digital services, identity and data platforms.
markets: Serves Saudi government and enterprise customers, with the Public Investment Fund as majority owner.
rationale: State-linked IT provider with Saudi focus; the Saudi Grand Prix offers hospitality, but the brand is not consumer-facing.

name: Enveda
desc: Biotech discovering medicines from natural compounds using machine learning and analytical chemistry.
markets: Based in Colorado; clinical-stage and pre-revenue, with no customers abroad.
rationale: Clinical-stage drug developer with no consumer brand to market; weak F1 fit.

name: Generalist AI
desc: Develops foundation models for robots to learn dexterous manipulation tasks.
markets: Research-stage company in California; no verified customers or international operations.
rationale: Early-stage robotics AI company with no consumer brand to market and no international audience; weak F1 fit.

name: Generate Biomedicines
desc: Biotechnology company using generative AI to design protein therapeutics such as antibodies.
markets: Based in Massachusetts; clinical-stage and pre-revenue, with no verified international operations.
rationale: Clinical-stage drug developer with no consumer brand to market and no commercial product; weak F1 fit.

name: Hark
desc: San Jose company said to develop multimodal AI software and agents; products and customers are unconfirmed.
markets: Based in California; products, customers and international activity are not confirmed.
rationale: Insufficient information about products or customers to judge any commercial F1 fit, so treated as weak.

name: Indra
desc: Spanish technology and defence group developing defence systems, air traffic management and IT consulting services.
markets: Customers in Spain, Europe, Latin America and other regions, across defence, transport and consulting.
rationale: Defence-heavy group with a B2B profile; Spanish Grand Prix hospitality and technology showcase fit, but defence ties limit marketing.

name: Lemonade
desc: Digital insurer using AI chatbots to sell and service renters, home, pet, car and life insurance.
markets: Sells insurance in the United States and parts of Europe.
rationale: Consumer-facing digital insurer wanting awareness among younger customers; F1 supports its US and European markets.

name: Oratomic
desc: Develops neutral-atom quantum hardware and error-correction technology, per its Crunchbase listing.
markets: Based in California; early-stage, with no verified customers or operations abroad.
rationale: Early-stage quantum hardware developer with no consumer brand to market and no confirmed customers; weak F1 fit.

name: OSL Group
desc: Hong Kong digital asset firm whose licensed OSL Digital Securities exchange offers crypto trading, brokerage and custody.
markets: Licensed in Hong Kong, serving retail and institutional clients mainly in Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Crypto brand seeking visibility in Asia; F1 has several crypto sponsors, but regulation restricts marketing.

name: OSL Group
desc: Hong Kong digital asset firm whose licensed OSL Digital Securities exchange offers crypto trading, brokerage and custody.
markets: Licensed in Hong Kong, serving retail and institutional clients mainly in Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Crypto brand seeking visibility in Asia; F1 has several crypto sponsors, but regulation restricts marketing.

name: Oxide Computer Company
desc: Builds rack-scale servers with integrated software for on-premises cloud computing.
markets: US start-up selling to enterprises; I cannot verify international customers.
rationale: Niche enterprise hardware vendor with a small marketing budget and mainly US customers; limited F1 fit.

name: Pateo
desc: Chinese automotive technology company providing connected-vehicle software, in-car infotainment and internet-of-vehicles services to carmakers.
markets: Based in Shanghai; sells to carmakers, mainly in China, with international reach I cannot verify.
rationale: B2B automotive supplier with low public awareness; technology showcase is plausible but F1 fit is limited.

name: Pathos
desc: Clinical-stage oncology company using AI and large patient datasets to develop cancer drugs.
markets: US-based drug developer; clinical-stage with no product sales or operations abroad.
rationale: Clinical-stage drug developer with no consumer brand to market and no commercial product; weak F1 fit.

name: Replit
desc: Cloud software development platform with a browser IDE and the Replit Agent AI tool that builds apps.
markets: Developers and non-developers worldwide use the platform online.
rationale: Fast-growing AI coding brand with a global online audience; F1 fits a technology showcase if budget allows.

name: Robot Era
desc: Chinese start-up developing general-purpose humanoid robots such as the STAR1 and related components.
markets: Chinese start-up with a Hong Kong location in the data; no verified overseas sales.
rationale: Early-stage robotics maker with no consumer brand to market and unverified overseas sales; weak F1 fit.

name: Runway
desc: Generative AI company building video and image generation tools and world models used by filmmakers and creators.
markets: Creators, studios and businesses worldwide use its tools online.
rationale: Creative-AI brand with a media audience; F1 content and its film-making tie-in offer a showcase.

name: Sharpa
desc: Singapore robotics start-up developing humanoid robots and components, especially dexterous robot hands and tactile sensing.
markets: Based in Singapore; sales and operations beyond Asia are unverified.
rationale: Early-stage robotics firm; Singapore Grand Prix gives a local showcase, but there is little brand marketing.

name: Sigma Computing
desc: Cloud analytics and business intelligence platform that lets business users explore and analyze data.
markets: Enterprise customers mainly in the United States, with customers in Europe and elsewhere.
rationale: Enterprise data-software brand; F1 hospitality and data showcase suit analytics peers, but awareness is niche.

name: Skydio
desc: Maker of autonomous AI-powered drones used by police, fire, military and infrastructure inspection customers.
markets: Sells drones to US and allied government and commercial customers in several regions.
rationale: Drone technology fits F1's engineering image, but its public-safety and defence customers limit consumer marketing.

name: Solace
desc: Software maker of the PubSub+ event streaming and management platform for enterprises.
markets: Enterprise customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, including financial and transport firms.
rationale: Enterprise middleware vendor with real-time data themes similar to F1; B2B hospitality is the main fit.

name: Spire Global
desc: Space-based data and analytics company operating small satellites for weather, maritime and aviation data.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia buying satellite data and analytics.
rationale: Data and weather analytics tie to F1 technology storytelling, though customers are specialist institutions.

name: Spirit AI
desc: Chinese embodied-AI start-up founded in 2024 building a general-purpose brain for humanoid and mobile robots.
markets: Beijing-based start-up; I cannot verify customers or overseas operations.
rationale: Early-stage embodied-AI firm with no consumer brand to market and unverified customers; weak F1 fit.

name: TARS Robotics
desc: Shanghai embodied-AI company working on AI-driven robots that operate in the physical world.
markets: Based in Shanghai; products, customers and overseas operations are not confirmed.
rationale: Early-stage robotics start-up with no verified brand marketing and unconfirmed customers; weak F1 fit.

name: Upstage
desc: AI company building large language models, including the Solar family, and document-processing AI such as Document Parse.
markets: Korean-founded; products used by enterprises in Korea, the US and other markets.
rationale: Enterprise AI vendor seeking international visibility; F1 suits a technology showcase if budget allows.

name: Upwind Security
desc: Cloud-native application protection platform that unifies cloud and application security to detect threats and risks.
markets: US and Israel-linked security vendor selling to enterprises; I cannot verify the customer mix.
rationale: Cybersecurity vendor in a category already present in F1; hospitality suits B2B sales, but awareness is limited.

name: Verkada
